question: On a lateral neck X-ray, epiglottitis produces the 'thumbprint sign' — a swollen, rounded epiglottis that resembles an adult thumb pressing down from the posterior pharyngeal wall — whereas croup produces the 'steeple sign' on an AP chest or neck X-ray.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Thumbprint sign = epiglottitis (swollen epiglottis on lateral X-ray). Steeple sign = croup (subglottic narrowing on AP X-ray). Memorise this pairing as it is a common exam and clinical vignette question. Crucially, in epiglottitis the X-ray should not be performed until after the airway is secured.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The thumbprint sign on lateral neck X-ray (an enlarged, rounded epiglottis) is pathognomonic of epiglottitis. The steeple sign (subglottic narrowing producing a church-steeple shape on AP film) is characteristic of croup. These two radiological signs serve as reliable distinguishing features — though remember, X-ray should only be obtained once the airway is secured in suspected epiglottitis.
